alyssa: Heads up — started seeing sporadic queue_wait spikes on /api/v1/chat-stream (hosted pool) around 22:04 UTC. P95 fine but P99 jumps from ~35ms -> ~220ms. :thinking:

mike: Can you paste the queue_wait histogram and the batch size distribution? wondering if scheduler is emitting lots of size=1 batches during those periods.

alyssa: Pasted snippets below. This was from the new prometheus scrape at 22:04:22. note the big bucket counts on 0.1-0.3s.
```
# runtime_scheduler_queue_wait_seconds_bucket{route="/api/v1/chat-stream",le="0.1"} 9452
# runtime_scheduler_queue_wait_seconds_bucket{route="/api/v1/chat-stream",le="0.3"} 12023
# runtime_batch_size_bucket{route="/api/v1/chat-stream",le="1"} 4300
# runtime_batch_size_bucket{route="/api/v1/chat-stream",le="4"} 15200
```

priya: hmm KV cache miss rate upticked around the same time after the kernel-change rollout (we switched to the tiled attention kernel for long seq). Miss ratio (kv_cache_miss_total / kv_cache_access_total) jumped from 0.04 -> 0.12. Could be eviction policy or small shifts in KV keys due to tensor layout changes.

sean: @alyssa @priya that lines up with the kernel selector fallthrough: when kernel A fails quantized path it falls back to slower kernel B and also bypasses some cache fast paths. We should correlate kernel_selection_failures metric with queue wait. Suggest adding label kernel=... to the existing metrics.

alyssa: Good call. I added a temporary gauge `runtime_kernel_selector_fallback_total{kernel_from=\"tiled\",kernel_to=\"fallback\"}` and saw 187 increments during the window. profiler-bot attached a flamegraph for one of the 220ms tails.

profiler-bot: Generated flamegraph for request 1779553229 at 22:04:29 -> https://artifacts/reports/fg-1779553229.svg (sampled 2s window). Key stack: scheduler::pop -> runtime::select_kernel -> op::attention_tiled -> memcpy -> kv_cache::lookup_slow_path.

mike: If memcpy + lookup_slow_path are in the tail, it suggests misaligned tensors trigger extra copies before KV lookup. Did the tiled kernel change the key dtype/layout?

priya: Yes — tiled kernel uses interleaved layout for keys. Our KV index expects contiguous layout; when layout mismatch we do a per-request transform and stash a temp buffer -> extra 50-120ms for large context. I can add a layout-hint to the cache key to avoid recomputing.

elaine: From dashboard perspective we need a token-level latency breakdown panel for the route: separate series for scheduling (queue_wait), batch_handling (batch_build + memcpy), kernel_exec, kv_lookup, and network. Proposal: add histogram metric `token_latency_bucket_seconds{stage=\"scheduler|batch_build|kernel|kv|network\",route=...}` and a Grafana waterfall per-request view.

sean: Also add per-route p50/p95/p99 for batch sizes with labels for kernel_variant and quantization_level. New metrics I want: `runtime_batch_size_histogram{route,kernel_variant}`, `runtime_scheduler_queue_wait_seconds{route,kernel_variant}`, `kv_cache_miss_ratio{route}` and `token_latency_breakdown_seconds_bucket{stage,route}`.

alyssa: Implemented `token_latency_breakdown_seconds` as a histogram with these buckets: [0.001,0.005,0.01,0.02,0.05,0.1,0.2,0.5,1.0]. Sample query to compute waterfall perc: 
```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_latency_breakdown_seconds_bucket{route="/api/v1/chat-stream",stage="kv"}[5m])) by (le))
```

mike: Nice. For the scheduler efficiency metric, let's derive a synthetic gauge: effective_throughput = tokens_emitted / (active_gpu_seconds) and scheduler_efficiency = emitted_vs_ideal where ideal assumes perfect packing. We can compute ideal tokens/emitted per batch size distribution. That helps quantify packing loss.

priya: One more thing — KV cache eviction settings: we had LRU shard size tuned for old layout. With tiled layout we get different key cardinality; raising per-shard capacity by 20% reduced miss ratio back down in my local repro. Patch coming.

alyssa: To be safe, rolling kernel change back for hosted-stable while infra + priya finish layout-hint + eviction tweak. Created revert: `deploy 2026-03-17T22:30 roll kernel/tiled -> kernel/mmapped-v2` and will watch metrics.

elaine: For dashboards: add a small per-route alert that fires when (p99 token_latency > 150ms AND kv_cache_miss_ratio > 0.08) for 5m. Also add an annotation when kernel selector rollout changes so we can tie spikes to deploys.

mike: Agreed. Also add a debug trace option in runtime to emit per-token timestamps for sampled requests (1/10000) — store in tracing bucket for 24h. That will let us reconstruct the waterfall without full payloads.

alyssa: OK plan: (1) revert kernel in hosted-stable (rolled) (2) priya lands layout-hint + eviction bump (3) seans' new metrics pushed and dashboards updated (4) enable sampled traces. I'll post a follow-up when we've got post-revert metrics. :thumbsup:

profiler-bot: Note: created incident placeholder INC-2026-0317-queue-wait for tracking and linked deploy and flamegraph artifacts.
